## Purpose and Scope

This RAD provides illustrative patterns and logical design guidance for securing containerized workloads — ECS (Fargate and EC2-backed) and EKS — across the Gainwell cloud environment.

**Governing ABBs**:
- [GUID-SEC-CLOUD-WORKLOAD-PROT-2.6.04 — Workload Protection](../GUID-SEC-CLOUD-WORKLOAD-PROT-2.6.04.md)
- [GUID-SEC-CLOUD-VULN-MGMT-2.6.09 — Vulnerability Management](../GUID-SEC-CLOUD-VULN-MGMT-2.6.09.md)
page_texts.4:
[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-CONTAINER-RAD-3.6.02.md#rad-scope]

### RAD Scope

- Container image build and scanning pipeline (CI/CD integration)
- ECR repository security: image scanning, image signing policy, lifecycle policy
- ECS task security: task role least-privilege, Fargate vs EC2 networking, secrets injection
- EKS cluster security: runtime monitoring, pod security standards, network policy
- GuardDuty runtime monitoring for containers
- Container workload isolation and incident response patterns

## Container Security Architecture Overview

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph CI_Pipeline["CI/CD Pipeline (Build Stage)"]
        BuildImage["Docker Build\nBase image: Amazon Linux 2023\nor Distroless"]
        ScanImage["Image Vulnerability Scan\nInspector / Trivy\nCritical CVE → FAIL pipeline"]

        ECRLifecycle["Lifecycle Policy\nRemove untagged images > 7 days\nKeep last N tagged versions"]
    end

    subgraph Runtime["Production Runtime — ECS / EKS"]
        subgraph ECS_Task["ECS Task (Fargate)"]
            TaskRole["Task IAM Role\nLeast-privilege\nNo wildcard permissions"]
            SecretsInject["Secrets Injection\nSecrets Manager reference\nNo env var plaintext"]
            FargateNet["Fargate Networking\nawsvpc mode\nSecurity group per task family"]
        end
        subgraph EKS_Pod["EKS Pod"]
            IRSA["IRSA (IAM Roles for\nService Accounts)\nPer-workload role binding"]
            PodSec["Pod Security Standards\nRestricted profile\nNo privileged containers"]
            NetworkPolicy["Network Policy\nAllow-list inter-pod communication\nDefault deny"]
        end
    end

    subgraph Detection["Runtime Detection"]
        GDRuntime["GuardDuty Runtime\nECS Runtime Monitoring\nEKS Runtime Monitoring"]

    end

    BuildImage --> ScanImage --> SignImage --> PushECR --> ECR
    ECR --> Runtime
    Runtime --> GDRuntime --> SecurityHub
```

[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-CONTAINER-RAD-3.6.02.md#base-image-standards]

### Base Image Standards

| Workload Type | Approved Base Images | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| JVM workloads | `amazoncorretto:21-al2023` | Minimal AL2023 with only JVM runtime |
| Python workloads | `public.ecr.aws/docker/library/python:3.12-slim` | Slim Debian with only Python runtime |
| Go / binary workloads | `gcr.io/distroless/base` | No shell, no package manager; minimal attack surface |
| Node.js workloads | `public.ecr.aws/docker/library/node:20-alpine` | Alpine-based; minimal package set |

Full OS base images (Ubuntu, Debian, RHEL) with extensive pre-installed packages **SHALL NOT** be used without documented justification.
page_texts.8:
[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-CONTAINER-RAD-3.6.02.md#pipeline-scan-gate]

### Pipeline Scan Gate

The CI/CD pipeline **SHALL** include a mandatory scan gate before push to ECR:

```
Build → Scan (Inspector/Trivy) → Gate Decision:
  ├── Critical CVE found → FAIL: block push, notify developer
  ├── High CVE found → WARNING: push allowed, create vulnerability ticket (SLA: 30 days)
  └── No Critical/High → PASS: push to ECR
```
page_texts.9:
[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-CONTAINER-RAD-3.6.02.md#ecr-repository-configuration]

### ECR Repository Configuration

- **Image scanning**: Enhanced scanning (Inspector v2) **SHALL** be enabled; basic scanning is insufficient
- **Image tag mutability**: `IMMUTABLE` **SHALL** be set; mutable tags allow silent image replacement
- **Repository policy**: Deny `*` principal; allow only specific account IAM roles for pull
- **Lifecycle policy**: Remove untagged images within 7 days; retain last 10 tagged production image versions

page_texts.11:
[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-CONTAINER-RAD-3.6.02.md#task-role-architecture]

### Task Role Architecture

```
ECS Task Definition
├── Task Role: arn:aws:iam::{acct}:role/prod-claims-ecs-task-role
│   ├── Permission Boundary: enterprise-workload-boundary
│   └── Inline/Managed Policies: ONLY permissions needed for THIS task
└── Execution Role: arn:aws:iam::{acct}:role/ecs-execution-role
    └── Permissions: ECR pull, CloudWatch Logs, Secrets Manager read for task bootstrap
```

**Task Role ≠ Execution Role**. The execution role is used by the ECS agent for infrastructure operations (pulling images, writing logs). The task role is used by the application code. They must be separate with separate least-privilege policies.
page_texts.14:
[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-CONTAINER-RAD-3.6.02.md#irsa-iam-roles-for-service-accounts]

### IRSA (IAM Roles for Service Accounts)

Each Kubernetes workload that needs AWS API access **SHALL** use IRSA rather than EC2 instance profile credentials:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: claims-processor
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::{acct}:role/prod-claims-processor-role
```

Node instance profiles **SHALL** have minimal permissions (SSM, ECR pull, CloudWatch). Application-level AWS access **SHALL** use IRSA only.
page_texts.15:
[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-CONTAINER-RAD-3.6.02.md#pod-security-standards]

### Pod Security Standards

All production namespaces **SHALL** enforce the `restricted` Pod Security Standard:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: production
  labels:
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce-version: latest
```

This prohibits: privileged containers, host network/PID/IPC, hostPath volumes, non-read-only root filesystems (strongly recommended), running as root.

### GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring

GuardDuty ECS and EKS Runtime Monitoring agents monitor syscall-level behavior within containers and detect:
- Process executing from unusual path (crypto mining pattern)
- Unusual outbound network connection to known-malicious IP
- Container breakout attempt (mounting host filesystem)
- Credential access from container (IMDS enumeration)
page_texts.18:
[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-CONTAINER-RAD-3.6.02.md#workload-isolation-pattern]

### Workload Isolation Pattern

When a GuardDuty Critical finding implicates a specific ECS task or EKS pod:

1. **Isolate**: Modify the security group attached to the task/ENI to deny all ingress/egress (preserve for forensics)
2. **Preserve**: Create EBS snapshot or task execution log export before termination
3. **Terminate**: Stop the compromised task/pod; ECS/EKS will replace with a clean instance from the image
4. **Investigate**: Review CloudTrail, VPC flow logs, and GuardDuty finding timeline for lateral movement indicators
5. **Remediate**: Rotate any credentials that may have been accessible to the compromised workload
